coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.distance_note: Piers 38 and 40, at the foot of King St/Townsend St (89 King St), sit about 420-460m north of Mission Rock's own tracked boundary (Pier 48/50), just north of and adjacent to South Beach Harbor.

record.summary: A long-stalled Port of San Francisco redevelopment of Piers 38 and 40, led by San Francisco Waterfront Partners III, LLC (SFWP); the Port's April 2026 memo calls Pacific Waterfront Partners an SFWP affiliate, while the Port's project page names Pacific Waterfront Partners as the negotiating party. The original Exclusive Negotiating Agreement (dated March 12, 2021) expired on March 15, 2023, and the Port's April 2026 memo says the developer is out of compliance with it because of missed Performance Dates. In April 2026 the Port Commission settled a related back-rent dispute and adopted an Amended and Restated ENA giving the developer a 12-month "Evaluation Period" to rework the project's scope and financing. The Registry SF reported on August 12, 2026 (publication date) that the piers "are being offered for long-term lease to major credit tenants"; that listing is not a lease or a Port-approved deal. No lease, term sheet or CEQA review is in place as of this record's last_verified date.

notes.accuracy_caveat: The outline is the union of Assessor lots 9900038 and 9900040, so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. Pier 38 is lot 9900038 and Pier 40 is lot 9900040 (DataSF lists both as active, block 9900, the pier number as the lot, street name KING), and the earlier traces lie 95% inside the two lots together, so the match is clear; no Port document read names the lots. Each lot's edge can run a few metres off the visible deck edge, and includes ground the traces left out (the Pier 38 bulkhead building along the Embarcadero and aprons); the lots are the legal boundaries. Status 'planned' means proposed only: the Port's April 28, 2026 staff report says the term sheet 'was never executed' and that the Port and developer agreed to 'suspend active negotiation of transaction documents' for twelve months 'to further evaluate project costs and other key obstacles to Project feasibility'; completing environmental (CEQA) analysis and executing a lease are still future benchmarks. Use is as shown on this record.

notes.why_no_real_parcel: Each pier has its own Assessor lot (Pier 38 is 9900038 and Pier 40 is 9900040; DataSF Parcels, acdm-wktn, active); this record is one project over two lots, and its outline is the two lots.
notes.regulatory_context: Developer: San Francisco Waterfront Partners III, LLC (SFWP), an affiliate of Pacific Waterfront Partners (PWP). Original Exclusive Negotiating Agreement: Port Commission Resolution 21-10 (2021-02-23), expired 2023-03-15 for missed performance dates. PWP separately owed the Port over $980,000 in back rent on three unrelated leases (Pier 28, two Agriculture Building suites), unpaid since it vacated them 2024-01-31. On 2026-04-28 the Port Commission adopted a Settlement Agreement (Resolution 26-21: PWP to pay $720,000 over 3 years, with the remainder of the debt forgiven on compliance) and an Amended and Restated ENA (Resolution 26-22: a 12-month 'Evaluation Period' to explore value engineering, project phasing and a new financial partner, with a new Schedule of Performance due before the period ends around April 2027). No lease, term sheet or CEQA review is in place as of this record's own last_verified date.

open_questions: No Port Commission agenda item after 2026-04-28 was found; the 12-month Evaluation Period runs to approximately April 2027 with an interim Schedule of Performance due before then -- worth a periodic re-check rather than treating April 2026 as the final word.
No current, authoritative square footage or cost figure exists for the project as of this record's last_verified date: the 2022 estimates are explicitly being re-evaluated under the 2026 Amended ENA.

No public official's or community/maritime-advocacy group's position on the 2026 Amended ENA or settlement specifically has been found and sourced (all community-input coverage found dates to the 2020 RFP era).

Given the project's history of default and its ongoing, unresolved Evaluation Period, its ultimate outcome is genuinely uncertain -- this record treats it as an active but fragile project worth continued tracking, not a settled one.

Who authorized the August 2026 marketing listing for Piers 38 & 40, and how it relates to the Port's Evaluation Period, is not stated in the readable part of The Registry SF's article (the rest is behind a paywall).

Developer of Piers 38 and 40: the Port's Calendar Item 9B memo (April 28, 2026) names San Francisco Waterfront Partners III, LLC (SFWP) and calls Pacific Waterfront Partners (PWP) an SFWP affiliate; the Port's project page (undated) and the San Francisco Chronicle (June 2, 2022) name Pacific Waterfront Partners as the developer.

2022 scope and cost: as last formally endorsed in 2022 and never executed, the scheme had approximately 215,000 sq ft office, up to 20,000 sq ft retail and approximately 130,000 sq ft public access/open space. The San Francisco Chronicle (June 2, 2022) gave a cost estimate of approximately $536 million; The Real Deal (July 14, 2022) said the developer "now estimates it will cost $528 million", up from an "initial estimate" of $383 million (no date given for that earlier estimate). These are estimates, not costs incurred, and are explicitly under review ("value engineering", "scope reduction") under the 2026 Amended ENA, so they are not current.

record.notes: The outline is Assessor lots 9900038 (Pier 38) and 9900040 (Pier 40) (see the accuracy note). The 2022 scope estimate (~215,000 sq ft office, up to 20,000 sq ft retail, ~$528-536M cost) is explicitly under review ('value engineering', 'scope reduction') per the April 2026 Amended ENA and is not treated as current. Separately, an August 2026 marketing listing ('Pacific Cornerstone') offers up to ~279,876 sq ft of the piers for long-term lease to credit tenants, positioning occupancy for late 2029 -- parallel tenant-marketing activity alongside the Port's own Evaluation Period, not a confirmed deal.
